title: Control Flag Propagation Complexity
pattern: Using an artificial boolean control flag (e.g., done) to control the flow and termination of a loop instead of early returns or breaks.
why_bad: The control flag complicates the control flow and forces the developer to trace how the flag changes and propagates across all branching conditions, increasing cognitive load and bug probability.
detection: A loop condition depends on a local boolean flag variable that is modified inside nested branch clauses of the loop body.
counterexample: Using direct break or return statements to exit immediately once the termination condition is met.
fix: Replace the control flag with a direct return or break statement to simplify the control flow: `if (condition) { return; }`.
